subproblem.title: Gluing: a current with a mass representation that agrees locally with integer multiplicity representations is integer multiplicity (IM is local)
subproblem.statement: Assume (IMC)(a), passed as a hypothesis: the exact first conjunct of the frozen statement of cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (hypothesis (IMC) of the selected node), namely: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and all Borel sets M ⊆ M' ⊆ U with Hⁿ(M' ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M and every linear subspace Q, Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x iff it is one of M' at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt). Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k), μ a Borel measure on ℝ^P and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k) such that μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). Suppose every x ∈ U lies in an open set W ⊆ U on which there is an IMRep R in W (IMRep W k) with μ⌞W = R.measure (the weight θ_R Hᵏ⌞M_R) and ξ(y) = R.orient(y) for μ-a.e. y ∈ W. Then X is integer multiplicity in U (IsIntegerMultiplicity X).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M M' : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet M → MeasurableSet M' → M ⊆ M' → M' ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (M' ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), IsOpen U → μ Uᶜ = 0 → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, X ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ) → (∀ x ∈ U, ∃ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep W k), IsOpen W ∧ x ∈ W ∧ W ⊆ U ∧ μ.restrict W = R.measure ∧ ∀ᵐ y ∂μ, y ∈ W → ξ y = R.orient y) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 7–9 of the selected node's proof (the gluing in Part I, T4 of the grandparent proof; Simon 6.3.1, chapter-06.txt lines 733–753, and the localization remark 8.3(1), lines 2311–2317). The selected proof equips the glued carrier with the local orientations ξ_{x_i}; since the hypotheses give ξ = ξ_{x_i} a.e. on each piece, we use ξ itself as the glued orientation, which reduces the representation step to an identity of measures. Uses the sibling imrep_measure. Notation: Hᵏ := μHE[k]; for an IMRep R write M_R, θ_R, ξ_R for R.carrier, R.mult, R.orient. By imrep_measure, for every IMRep R (in any set): (b) Hᵏ⌞M_R ≪ R.measure; (c) R.measure(A) = ∫_{M_R∩A} θ_R dHᵏ for every Borel A; (g) R.action ω = ∫ ξ_R(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) for every k-form ω.
1. The case U = ∅. Then μ(ℝ^P) = μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, so X(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ = 0 for every ω. The IMRep in U with carrier ∅, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 represents X: ∅ is Borel, ∅ ⊆ U, ∅ is countably k-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero), the multiplicity is measurable, the positivity condition is vacuous, every integral over ∅ is 0 (this gives local integrability and action 0 = X(ω)), and Hᵏ⌞∅ = 0, so the measurability and orientation conditions hold trivially. From now on U ≠ ∅.
2. Countable subcover. For each x ∈ U choose an open W_x ⊆ U with x ∈ W_x and an IMRep R_x in W_x as in the hypothesis. The open sets W_x (x ∈ U) cover U and ℝ^P is second countable, so there is a countable set T ⊆ U with ⋃_{x∈T} W_x = ⋃_{x∈U} W_x = U (Lindelöf; Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable). T ≠ ∅ because U ≠ ∅, so T = {x_0, x_1, x_2, …} for a sequence (x_i)_{i∈ℕ} (Set.Countable.exists_eq_range; repetitions allowed). Write W_i := W_{x_i}, R_i := R_{x_i}, and M_i, θ_i, ξ_i for the carrier, multiplicity and orientation of R_i. Then each W_i is open, W_i ⊆ U, ⋃_i W_i = U, M_i ⊆ W_i, μ⌞W_i = R_i.measure, and ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) for μ-a.e. y ∈ W_i.
3. Disjoint pieces. Put A_i := W_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} W_j (Mathlib disjointed). The A_i are Borel, pairwise disjoint, A_i ⊆ W_i, and ⋃_i A_i = ⋃_i W_i = U.
4. Glued data. Let M := ⋃_i (M_i ∩ A_i) and define θ : ℝ^P → ℕ by θ(y) := θ_i(y) if y ∈ A_i (the index i is unique) and θ(y) := 0 if y ∉ U (for instance θ(y) := θ_{n(y)}(y) with n(y) the least n such that y ∈ A_n, Nat.find, and θ(y) := 0 if there is no such n). Then: (i) M is Borel and M ⊆ U (M_i ⊆ W_i ⊆ U); since the A_i are pairwise disjoint, M ∩ A_i = M_i ∩ A_i for every i. (ii) θ is measurable: it takes values in the countable set ℕ, and for every m ∈ ℕ, θ⁻¹({m}) = ⋃_i (A_i ∩ θ_i⁻¹({m})) ∪ E_m with E_m := ℝ^P ∖ U if m = 0 and E_m := ∅ otherwise, a countable union of Borel sets (Mathlib measurable_to_countable'). (iii) θ = θ_i on A_i; in particular θ(y) = θ_i(y) ≥ 1 for y ∈ M_i ∩ A_i, so θ ≥ 1 on M. (iv) M is countably k-rectifiable: each M_i ∩ A_i ⊆ M_i is (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono), and so is the countable union (countablyRectifiable_iUnion).
5. The measure identity μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ. Let S be Borel. The sets S ∩ A_i are Borel and pairwise disjoint with union S ∩ U, and μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0. Since S ∩ A_i ⊆ W_i and μ⌞W_i = R_i.measure, μ(S ∩ A_i) = μ(S ∩ A_i ∩ W_i) = R_i.measure(S ∩ A_i). Using imrep_measure (c) for R_i, then (i) and (iii): μ(S) = μ(S ∩ U) = Σ_i μ(S ∩ A_i) = Σ_i R_i.measure(S ∩ A_i) = Σ_i ∫_{M_i ∩ S ∩ A_i} θ_i dHᵏ = Σ_i ∫_{M ∩ S ∩ A_i} θ dHᵏ = ∫_{M∩S} θ dHᵏ, the last step by countable additivity of the lower integral over the pairwise disjoint Borel sets M ∩ S ∩ A_i, whose union is M ∩ S because M ⊆ U = ⋃_i A_i (Mathlib lintegral_iUnion). Finally ∫_{M∩S} θ dHᵏ = ((Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ)(S) (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). Two measures that agree on all Borel sets are equal, so μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ.
6. Consequences. (a) For compact K ⊆ U (closed, hence Borel), ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ = μ(K) < ∞ by step 5. (b) Since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hᵏ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. (c) θ ≠ 0 holds Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. (θ ≥ 1 on M, and Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. point lies in the Borel set M), so Hᵏ⌞M ≪ (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ = μ (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous'). (d) ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac with (c)).
7. Orientation. Fix i and put N_i := M_i ∩ A_i = M ∩ A_i (Borel). (α) By the field orients of R_i, for Hᵏ⌞M_i-a.e. y there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_i y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ_i(y)) Q; since N_i ⊆ M_i this holds for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y (ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset). (β) By hypothesis ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) for μ-a.e. y ∈ W_i, i.e. for (μ⌞W_i)-a.e. y (ae_restrict_iff', W_i Borel), i.e. for R_i.measure-a.e. y. By imrep_measure (b), Hᵏ⌞M_i ≪ R_i.measure, so ξ = ξ_i holds Hᵏ⌞M_i-a.e., hence Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. (γ) Apply (IMC)(a) in the open set W_i to the Borel sets N_i ⊆ M_i ⊆ W_i. Its local finiteness hypothesis holds: for compact K ⊆ W_i, Hᵏ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M_i∩K} θ_i dHᵏ < ∞, because θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i and R_i is locally integrable in W_i (field locallyIntegrable_mult). So for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k N_i y Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_i y Q. (δ) Apply (IMC)(a) in the open set U to the Borel sets N_i ⊆ M ⊆ U, with local finiteness from 6(b): for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k N_i y Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M y Q. Intersecting these four full-measure sets: for Hᵏ⌞N_i-a.e. y, the subspace Q from (α) is an approximate tangent space of N_i at y by (γ), hence of M at y by (δ), and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q holds because ξ(y) = ξ_i(y) by (β). Since M = ⋃_i N_i is a countable union, the property 'there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q' holds for Hᵏ⌞M-a.e. y (Mathlib ae_restrict_iUnion_iff).
8. The glued IMRep. R := (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U: measurableSet_carrier and carrier_subset by 4(i), rectifiable by 4(iv), measurable_mult by 4(ii), mult_pos by 4(iii), locallyIntegrable_mult by 6(a), aestronglyMeasurable_orient by 6(d), and orients by step 7. By definition R.measure = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ, which equals μ by step 5.
9. Representation. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), imrep_measure (g) applied to R gives R.action ω = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dR.measure(x) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) = X(ω). So R represents X, and X is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: If U = ∅ then μ = 0 and the empty IMRep represents X.
Choose the local data (W_x, R_x); by Lindelöf take a countable subcover (W_i) and the disjoint Borel pieces A_i := W_i ∖ ⋃_{j<i} W_j, which cover U.
Glue M := ⋃_i (M_i ∩ A_i) and θ := θ_i on A_i (0 off U): M is Borel and countably k-rectifiable, θ is measurable and θ ≥ 1 on M.
μ⌞W_i = R_i.measure, imrep_measure (c) and countable additivity give μ = (Hᵏ⌞M).withDensity θ; hence local integrability of θ and Hᵏ⌞M ≪ μ, so ξ is Hᵏ⌞M-measurable.
Take ξ as glued orientation: ξ = ξ_i Hᵏ-a.e. on M_i ∩ A_i (imrep_measure (b)), and (IMC)(a) in W_i and in U shows that the approximate tangent spaces of M_i, M_i ∩ A_i and M agree a.e. there.
R.action ω = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ = X(ω) by imrep_measure (g), so X is integer multiplicity.

audit.reason: The countable partition constructs a measurable rectifiable carrier and positive measurable multiplicity. The measure identity establishes compact finiteness before both tangent-locality applications, avoiding circularity. Absolute continuity transfers orientation measurability and equality correctly; imrep_measure supplies the final action identity. The empty-domain case and every IMRep field are covered, and the parent's proof discharges these exact local hypotheses.
